summary:
India seeks RoDTEP and RoSCTL extensions beyond December 31, with ₹23,000 crore (~$2.46 billion) sought for RoDTEP.
Budget allocations fall to ₹10,000 crore and ₹5,000 crore, respectively; an Export Promotion Mission merger is proposed.
US-bound RoSCTL shipments fell 19.4 per cent to $4.14 billion in January–July 2026, accounting for 88 per cent of the segment’s decline.

title: Lyocell prices split: China weakens, India firms on cost support
summary:
Lyocell staple fibre diverged across Asia over three weeks, with India rising and China slipping as the India-China price gap widened by about 28 per cent.
Chinese offers moved from $2.131/kg to $2.121/kg, while Indian prices climbed from $2.293/kg to $2.328/kg.
Dissolving pulp stayed flat, leaving China with a thinner fibre-over-pulp spread.

title: India cotton yarn steady amid weak demand; Gujarat prices fall
summary:
India’s Mumbai and Tiruppur cotton yarn prices stayed stable as sluggish post-Diwali demand and tight payment flows kept textile trading sentiment weak.
Spinning mills resisted price cuts, helped by school uniform material demand, while traders expect bearish conditions to persist near term.
Gujarat cotton eased by ₹500–800 (~$5.4–8.6) per candy as new-season arrivals rose and ICE futures declined.

title: US cotton export sales weaken, Upland shipments hit new low
summary:
US cotton export sales weakened in the week ended November 12, 2026, with Upland sales down 25 per cent to 118,700 RB and shipments at a marketing-year low of 117,800 RB. 
Turkiye led Upland buying with 45,800 RB, while Vietnam was the top shipment destination at 44,200 RB. 
Pima sales were 80 per cent above the four-week average, led by India.

title: Germany's producer price inflation hits 3-year high of 8.1% in Oct
summary:
Germany’s industrial producer prices rose 8.1 per cent year on year in October 2026, marking the largest increase since February 2023, driven mainly by an 18.7 per cent surge in energy prices amid the Iran and Middle East conflict. 
Prices also increased 1.4 per cent month on month, while producer prices excluding energy rose 3.6 per cent annually, Destatis said.

title: US cotton futures recover but remain under pressure
summary:
US cotton futures recovered modestly on November 19, with March 2027 up 0.80 per cent at 79.51 cents per pound, but still 310 points lower for the week.
USDA data showed current-year Upland net sales fell 25 per cent week on week and 44 per cent below the four-week average.
A stronger US dollar, liquidation and cautious risk appetite kept sentiment bearish.

title: VIATT 2027 names Thailand as inaugural Partner Country
summary:
Thailand will be VIATT’s inaugural Partner Country when the fair returns to Vietnam from 24–26 February 2027.
A Thai pavilion, product displays, fashion show, seminars and networking events will showcase its textile and fashion capabilities.
Eight other country and region pavilions and zones will strengthen the international offering across apparel, home textiles and technical textile technologies.

title: Drewry WCI falls 3% as Transpacific rates ease
summary:
Drewry’s World Container Index fell 3 per cent to $4,176 per FEU in the week ending November 12 as Transpacific routes weakened.
Shanghai–New York rates dropped 9 per cent and Shanghai–Los Angeles fell 5 per cent, with carriers adding blank sailings amid weak demand.
Drewry expects Transpacific declines, but Asia–Europe rates may rise in December on stronger demand and peak season surcharges.

title: 48.9% profit margin: Can Japan's textile giants win the AI boom?
summary:
Japan’s spinning groups are earning higher margins in AI-linked materials, with Nittobo electronic materials at 48.9 per cent and Fujibo polishing pads at 27.8 per cent in April to September 2026.
TexPro shows HS 5911 exports fell 22.0 per cent from 2022 to 2025, while HS 5603 nonwovens dropped 7.8 per cent.
Early 2026 data show selective gains, but broad categories still slipped.

title: South Africa's $295 mn sourcing puzzle: Who makes the uniforms?
summary:
South Africa’s Treasury is reviewing government clothing and uniform specifications as analysis highlights a modelled R5.11 billion opportunity for additional local sourcing.
A Localisation Support Fund study verified 32 per cent of estimated public textile and clothing spend as reaching compliant domestic suppliers; 68 per cent was unconfirmed or non-local.

title: 26% of Canada's apparel imports: What's at stake by 2032?
summary:
Bangladesh's LDC graduation has been deferred to November 2029, which could extend Canada's duty-free apparel access until November 2032.
Cambodia could retain similar benefits until December 2032; the two accounted for about 26 per cent of Canada's apparel imports by value in 2025.
Without LDCT or another preference, high-volume garments face MFN duties of 17-18 per cent, raising sourcing risk.

title: US' Gap Inc appoints Ashley Kechter as Athleta CEO from December 14
summary:
Gap Inc has appointed Ashley Kechter as brand president and chief executive officer of Athleta, effective December 14, reporting to president and CEO Richard Dickson.
Kechter joins from Vuori, where she was global president, and has also led Fabletics.
Her experience spans apparel, activewear, sourcing, supply chain, merchandising and international expansion.

title: Cambodia's $10.22 bn apparel exports: Can growth last into 2027?
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports reached a record $10.22 billion in January-October 2026, up 6.31 per cent year on year; garments accounted for 34.1 per cent of merchandise shipments.
Knitted apparel rose 4.3 per cent and woven apparel 10.9 per cent, while shipments to the US rose as its apparel imports fell.
Imported fabric dependence and US tariff rules pose risks for buyers and manufacturers.

title: Bangladesh plans $3.5 mn post-LDC trade push
summary:
Bangladesh plans a $3.5 million, three-year push to strengthen trade competitiveness after least developed country graduation, according to the commerce ministry. 
About $2.5 million is proposed for seven priority areas in the WTO's EIF Phase Three project. 
Areas cover AI market forecasts, processed food, geographical indication goods, trade facilitation, ESG, carbon markets and negotiation training.

title: Bangladesh's CPD proposes new pay benchmarks for RMG workers
summary:

Its benchmarks cover inflation, the urban Dhaka poverty line and a living-wage basket for a four-member household with 1.58 earners.
The wage board meets on November 23; workers seek Tk32,000 (~$257), while owners have not filed a proposal.

title: Turkiye’s growing role in Bangladesh’s market diversification drive
summary:

Turkiye drove the increase, with shipments surging 107.05 per cent to $206.5 million and accounting for an estimated 53 per cent of overall growth.
Japan remained the top non-traditional market; India fell.

title: Egypt gains 29.1% in EU apparel: Can it challenge Turkiye by 2027?
summary:

EU clothing imports from Egypt reached €689 million in 2025, up 17.2 per cent year on year and 48 per cent from 2022; January–June 2026 imports were put at $747 million, up 29.1 per cent.
Egypt targets garment exports of about $12 billion by 2030.

title: Bangladesh basics account for 97% of apparel export growth in July-Oct
summary:

Total apparel exports rose 5.82 per cent to $13.75 billion from $12.99 billion a year earlier.
High-value products grew just 0.67 per cent to $1.86 billion, cutting their share to 13.54 per cent.

title: Hong Kong's apparel imports fall 4.4%, China's share declines
summary:

China remained the top supplier, but shipments declined 13 per cent to $1.833 billion.
Italy, Vietnam, France and Japan increased shipments, signalling broader sourcing diversification in 2026.

title: India’s apparel exports to US fall 20.5%: Can it win back buyers?
summary:
India’s readymade garment exports rose 20.33 per cent year on year to $1.287 billion in October 2026, but April-October exports remained 2.97 per cent lower and US-bound shipments fell sharply.
The rebound follows a weak October 2025 base, with the latest value only 4.8 per cent above October 2024.
No India-specific US tariff advantage is confirmed without an implemented apparel schedule.
